To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of a loyalty program depends on the firm’s market share and the market saturation level, and that the impact of market saturation on the program’s performance varies with category expandability.

the impact of a loyalty program is positively related to a firm’s market share, and that it is negatively related to the level of market saturation when the product category’s demand is rigid but not when the category is expandable.
larger firms benefit more than smaller firms from their loyalty program, and the impact of a firm’s loyalty program decreases when the product category’s demand becomes rigid.

the impact of market saturation on a loyalty program’s effectiveness.
the competitive implications of loyalty program offerings and provides insights on how to effectively manage such offerings in a competitive setting.
the impact of market saturation on the effectiveness of a single loyalty program.

the performance of a loyalty program is a function of a firm’s market share, market saturation, and category expandability.
the impact of loyalty programs depends on market saturation, market share, and category expandability.
loyalty program competition is more intense in a rigid category, but less intense in an expandable one.
